steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch casserole dish.

Sauté butter and onion in a medium saucepan over medium heat until onion is translucent, 3 to 4 minutes. Add salt, pepper, basil, brown sugar, and tomatoes; mix well. Stir in bread until well combined. Pour tomato-bread mixture into the prepared dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes. Enjoy.

raw_recipe.headline: Scalloped Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: These scalloped tomatoes are made with basil, brown sugar, bread cubes, and onions cooked with thick, juicy slices of tomato and baked in the oven until your kitchen smells wonderful.
raw_recipe.name: Scalloped Tomatoes

review.reviewBody:
I served this recipe to a large group and it was a hugh success. I also made it
one day ahead and chilled until ready to bake. I used a sour dough bread and 
1/4 cup fresh basil rather than dry. I also sprinkled a parmesan, romano and 
asiago mixture on top. I will definately make this again.

I made the recipe as directed but I did use seasoned croutons as others had suggested. I also added minced fresh garlic, a handful of fresh herbs - basil, thyme and oregano from my garden. I also mixed some feta cheese into the mixture. It was very Mediterranean tasting! Yum!

Scaled this down to 3 servings, used very ripe Campari tomatoes, cut each in half vertically through the center and then into slices. I cut my bread into 1/2-inch cubes. I checked at 25 minutes, they were starting to brown nicely, so I took them out of the oven. My tomatoes were very juicy, just right for scalloped tomatoes, and they cooked up beautifully. The texture on this was just about perfect, it was tasty, moist, and certainly quick-and-easy to make. A 5-star side dish.

Linda! You! Your mother! GENIUS!! I have so many ripe, Roma tomatoes in my garden; this was an EXCELLENT recipe to use them up. Since I had a bounty of Romas but the recipe calls for a 9x13 baking dish, I chopped approximately 3c tomatoes. I also added some freshly minced garlic the last few minutes to the onion sauté (sautéd onions for about 4 min, and another 3 min with the garlic). I had some spinach I had to use up so threw that in when adding the tomatoes but before tossing in the cubes of sourdough bread. Used 1 tsp of basil but left the brown sugar as written. I think fresh basil would work well here too. Baked for 30 min - which was perfect. A superb side dish to the grilled pork chops! Already shared this recipe with my mom and plan to make again next week! Thanks for sharing this! A winner!

This is a fabulous recipe. I made it as directed. I used a crusty bakery-style roasted garlic bread. To keep it from getting soggy, I put the tomato mixture in the 9x13 pan and placed the bread cubes on top to get kind of crispy in the oven. Three of us finished one recipe as a side dish to ocean perch, fresh corn on the cob, and cucumbers I had placed in a homemade vinaigrette. Magnificent. Thanks for this wonderful recipe. I will make it again and again while I have so many tomatoes. I'm sure this would be good with canned tomatoes as well.
I used fresh basil and sourdough bread. I only used 3 Tbsp. of brown sugar. It was a delicious way to use up my many tomatoes 🍅 😋

This is a recipe often found throughout Italy - with a few adjustments. Olive oil in place of butter, fresh basil in place of dried, day old bread made into croutons in place of bread, garlic added to the onion saute, Romano cheese added to mixture, & topped off with mozzarella cheese. Drizzle lightly with extra-virgin olive oil when it comes out of the oven & you are all set!

Was easy to do. Took the advice from other reviewers and add minced garlic, used seasoned dry croutons, and toped with parmesan cheese for the last 10 minutes. Next time I think I shall try a sharp cheddar instead of parmesan. Oh and use a 9X9 pan instead of the 9x13.

Really good and a great way to use up old bread and ends of tomatoes. I had extra tops and bottoms along with a slice of ciabatta that worked very well without pre-toasting. Parmesan was added at the baking stage and some mozzarella the last 10 minutes which I would definitely do again. The dish was put together early in the day and refrigerated, but baking it uncovered made a great consistency for us. Thanks for the recipe - we'll use it regularly.
This was quick, easy and GOOD. I’d make the again. I used seasoned croutons and added 1 teaspoon of garlic powder and some Parmesan cheese to the mixture and also lightly sprinkled on top.

I can’t believe I’ve never reviewed this dish! I have been making it for years and it is always a crowd pleaser. I also use croutons and add garlic, and less sugar. I love the flavor of basil too so I put a bit more in there. This dish is excellent.
Finally- my Mom's recipe exactly. Ate leftovers for breakfast with a sunny-side up egg and bacon.

Since cooking for 2, I halved the recipe. I used gluten-free bread and plant-based stick for the recipe. Good way to use up fresh tomatoes. I will be taking this to the next neighborhood potluck with a full recipe.

I made this as written, and it was fantastic. I tried using croutons made from day old cornbread. This adds so much goodness! I cut down on the sugar added to 1 tablespoon since the cornbread was already sweet. I am doing it tomorrow for Thanksgiving. It should will be a great addition to the meal.

Very good! Like others I used seasoned croutons but didn’t have quite enough for two cups so made up the difference with crushed ritz crackers. I only used one and a half tsps of sugar and it was plenty for our taste. Everything fit into my oval casserole dish (10x7x3”). Easy and tasty recipe!

I love this dish! Absolutely delicious! I followed the recipe only swapping the dried basil with fresh basil. Very easy recipe to make. I would have never thought of this combination. I have never seen a recipe like this. Thank you for sharing. This time of year with so many tomatoes in my garden it's nice to try something new. I've canned enough sauce & salsa to last the year. Again thank you

I cook it this time on top of range instead of in the oven. IT was really good & everyone liked it. Had to stir more than I wanted but with sugar it wanted to stick. Cook it in an covered Cast Irin pot with enamel I should have use Stainless Steel or Non Stuck Pot & I probably wouldnt have this problem. It was so good my daughter would heat up left over & eat them by thereself.

This recipe is excellent especially for those who have a bounty of tomatoes like me. I do however agree with almost all the additions people mentioned. I added one garlic clove and the slivered parmesan cheese but mixed it in. However, next time I make this recipe, I will reduce or modify the amount of brown sugar to the kind of tomato I will use. It tasted a little too sweet for my taste, but as for everything else, the recipe is just downright good. If I use more acid tomatoes definitely will stick with the 4 tsps. of sugar. If the tomatoes are on the sweet side, then I will just add half the sugar the recipe calls for. Will definitely make it again! EDIT: Made this recipe again with half the sugar and a bit more acid tomatoes than the first time...Will reduce the sugar to 1tsp. Also, this is a great recipe to use up "day old" bread! This recipe has saved a lot of leftover baguettes and big loaves of bread already!
This recipe reminded me of another favorite of mine, Panzenella which is the cold version of this recipe.
I loved this as a starting point. I added celery and garlic with the onion and then added some oregano with the basil.
